additional_concerns: Footnote 4 is supplied at db43e253bea18.u30.8235; the advertising claim incorrectly describes it as missing. The incorporated Advertising Guidelines and supplementary FAQs and guidance remain missing.

Detailed gift classification requires the applicable Code of Conduct paragraph 3.11 and the answer to question 1 of the SFC FAQs issued on 30 September 2010, referenced by footnotes 2 and 3. Can these external authorities be supplied? No supplied dependency IDs identify them.

Scope placement changes answers. node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e returns OUT_OF_SCOPE for an unoffered component; node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f does so for absence of linked offering; both offer-level candidates do so when promotional scope fails. For an otherwise in-scope distributor, the typed prohibition questions could instead require FALSE. Intentional assessment prerequisites and misplaced substantive conditions remain unresolved alternatives.

node.6d6e7adc6faa9d94b74c08e5 returns OUT_OF_SCOPE without a promotional link. A broader selected-control compliance interpretation could instead require TRUE because prohibited conduct is absent. Neither interpretation establishes overall regulatory compliance.

Scope placement also changes uncertainty propagation. With distributor status TRUE, offering UNKNOWN and gift classification FALSE, node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249 can return FALSE while node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e returns UNKNOWN. Agreement on fully known, in-scope facts does not establish executable equivalence.

The offer-level candidates combine an offer-wide promotional link with an existential non-discount gift classification. Different components could satisfy these conditions in a mixed offer, creating an unsupported prohibition. An explicit same-component connection or an established invariant that relevant components share the promotion is needed.

The introductory distributor definition supports the circular's SFC-authorised-fund context. Paragraph 3.11's quoted investment-product language is broader; fund-specific candidate definitions do not establish its exhaustive external scope.

node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b makes offer attribution explicit, but the source does not establish complete rules for third-party funding or fulfilment. Offering need not await completed receipt or payment; detailed attribution remains unchecked.

Paragraph 9 says returns or incentives may be gifts, not that they automatically are. A discount in one component does not exempt a distinct gift. Actual distraction, public invitation and aggressive marketing are not stated prerequisites to the gift restriction.
The supplied text establishes no operative date interval. The referenced FAQ date does not establish the circular's effective interval.

These 12 pairwise findings retain the supported separate controls. NOT_APPLICABLE neither validates the complete gift implementations nor authorizes pruning. Missing external authorities limit detailed interpretation without negating the circular's express summaries; the supplied representations do not verify implemented classifiers or runtime code.
